falsifier: Any function where moving a store through an addressed local array across a use of a SIBLING element leaves both the reload count and the callee-saved save set unchanged -- concretely, `python tools/gdl/probe.py <unit> <fn> --ops --no-slots` returning the same instruction count and the same opcode multiset delta for the barrier-before, barrier-between and barrier-after arrangements. For the mb_camera instance specifically: if `python tools/gdl/probe.py game/mb/mb_camera.c MBWorldToScreen3D --ops --no-slots` at the committed 3-before/1-after arrangement ever reads T104/O102 with `target-only: +1 lfd +1 stfd` again, the barrier is not what produced the pair and this law is disproved on its own headline instance. The law is also disproved by any counterexample where the compiler is shown to CSE the element across the sibling store (one load serving uses on both sides), since the whole mechanism rests on the barrier being unconditional for same-array elements.
subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: A store through an ADDRESSED local array is a CSE barrier for loads of OTHER elements of the SAME array, and the count of uses left on each side of that barrier decides two things at once: how many times the element is reloaded, and whether the allocator reaches past the volatiles into a CALLEE-SAVED FPR. The barrier is positional in SOURCE, and the barrier's position is the lever -- not the loads, not the uses, and not any naming of the operands. MEASURED on game/mb/mb_camera.c::MBWorldToScreen3D across three probes at commit c7b741799, all at -O4 with the demo cflags. The function reads `projected[2]` four times and stores `projected[0]` and `projected[1]`; `projected` is passed to vec4ApplyTrans so it is memory-resident. With the `projected[0]` store BEFORE the third and fourth reads (the state that had stood for five lanes), ours emitted two loads splitting the uses 2-before/2-after and THIRTEEN distinct FPRs, f0-f13 with f13 never used, at insns T104/O102 and an opcode multiset delta of exactly `target-only: +1 lfd +1 stfd` -- the missing f31 save pair. Moving the store PAST both remaining reads (uses 4-before/0-after) collapsed the CSE to a SINGLE load: O101, `target-only: +1 lfd +1 lfs +1 stfd`, real 84 -> 125. Moving it to sit BETWEEN the third and fourth reads (3-before/1-after, which is the target's own split) produced the save pair immediately: `stfd f31` and `lfd f31` appeared, insns went T104/O104, the opcode multiset went IDENTICAL, and fuzzy went 78.8654% -> 88.1346% once the frame was trimmed to match. The three arrangements differ ONLY in where one assignment statement sits. Two consequences worth carrying. FIRST, the count of uses after the barrier is readable in the TARGET before any probe: count that element's loads and which uses each one feeds in the aligned view, and the barrier's source position follows. SECOND, this is the mechanism to reach for when a residual is a missing callee-saved FP save pair and the pressure account has already been refuted -- on this function a live-FP census (10-11 values live against 14 free volatiles) and ten probes across four lanes on pressure-raising and promotion-forcing constructs all left the save pair untouched, because the pair was never a pressure question; it was a question of how long ONE cse'd load has to stay live, and the barrier sets that. The same edit also restored the TU's `extab` and `extabindex` sections from 97.9167%/98.6111% to 100.0000%, i.e. count parity paid in matched DATA as well as text.
